DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93, Module 4.

Terminal objective

1.0 Without references, DESCRIBE the construction and operation of a given type of valve, valve component, or valve actuator, as presented in this module. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.vii

Enabling objectives

1.1 DESCRIBE the four basic types of flow control elements employed in valve design. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.vii

1.2 DESCRIBE how valve stem leakage is controlled. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.vii

1.3 Given a drawing of a valve, IDENTIFY the following: DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.vii

  • a. Body
  • b. Bonnet
  • c. Stem
  • d. Actuator
  • e. Packing
  • f. Seat
  • g. Disk

1.4 Given a drawing of a valve, IDENTIFY each of the following types of valves: DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.vii

  • a. Globe
  • b. Gate
  • c. Plug
  • d. Ball
  • e. Needle
  • f. Butterfly
  • g. Diaphragm
  • h. Pinch
  • i. Check
  • j. Stop check
  • k. Safety/relief
  • l. Reducing

1.5 DESCRIBE the application of the following types of valves: DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.vii

  • a. Globe
  • b. Gate
  • c. Plug
  • d. Ball
  • e. Needle
  • f. Butterfly
  • g. Diaphragm
  • h. Pinch
  • i. Check
  • j. Safety/relief
  • k. Reducing

1.6 DESCRIBE the construction and principle of operation for the following types of valve actuators: DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.vii

  • a. Manual
  • b. Electric motor
  • c. Pneumatic
  • d. Hydraulic
  • e. Solenoid

What valves do

Objectives 1.1

"A valve is a mechanical device that controls the flow of fluid and pressure within a system or process." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.1
  • Stopping and starting fluid flow
  • Varying (throttling) the amount of fluid flow
  • Controlling the direction of fluid flow
  • Regulating downstream system or process pressure
  • Relieving component or piping over pressure

DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.1

"In general, there are four methods of controlling flow through a valve." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.6
  • Move a disc or plug into or against an orifice, as in a globe or needle valve
  • Slide a flat, cylindrical, or spherical surface across an orifice, as in gate and plug valves
  • Rotate a disc or ellipse about a shaft across the diameter of an orifice, as in a butterfly or ball valve
  • Move a flexible material into the flow passage, as in diaphragm and pinch valves

DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.6

Knowledge check: What valves do

Objective 1.1Q1436

Which is one of the four basic methods of controlling flow through a valve?

The answer is D. The four methods are moving a disc or plug against an orifice, sliding a surface across an orifice, rotating a disc or ellipse about a shaft, and moving a flexible material into the flow passage. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.6

Report a problem
Objective 1.1Q1437

Which flow control method does a butterfly valve use?

The answer is D. Rotating a disc or ellipse about a shaft extending across the diameter of an orifice applies to a butterfly or ball valve. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.6

Basic valve parts

Objectives 1.2, 1.3

"Regardless of type, all valves have the following basic parts: the body, bonnet, trim (internal elements), actuator, and packing." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.1
"The body, sometimes called the shell, is the primary pressure boundary of a valve." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.2

The body resists fluid pressure loads from connecting piping and receives the piping through threaded, bolted, or welded joints. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.2

"The cover for the opening in the valve body is the bonnet." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.3

The bonnet is the second principal pressure boundary, and it is a potential source of leakage. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.3

"The internal elements of a valve are collectively referred to as a valve's trim" DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.3

The trim typically includes a disk, seat, stem, and sleeves that guide the stem. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.3

"The disk provides the capability for permitting and prohibiting fluid flow." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.3
"The seat or seal rings provide the seating surface for the disk." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.3

The stem connects the actuator and disk. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.4

"connects the actuator and disk, is responsible for positioning the disk." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.4
"For a rising stem valve, the stem will rise above the actuator as the valve is opened." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.4

A nonrising stem shows no upward movement outside the valve. The disk is threaded internally and travels on the stem. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.5

"The actuator operates the stem and disk assembly." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.5
"Most valves use some form of packing to prevent leakage from the space between the stem and the bonnet." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.5
"If a valve's packing is too loose, the valve will leak, which is a safety hazard. If the packing is too tight, it will impair the movement and possibly damage the stem." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.5

Objective 1.3Q1438

Which part is the primary pressure boundary of a valve?

The answer is A. The body, sometimes called the shell, is the primary pressure boundary of a valve. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.2

Report a problem
Objective 1.3Q1439

What is the purpose of the valve stem?

The answer is C. The stem connects the actuator and disk and is responsible for positioning the disk. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.4

Report a problem
Objective 1.2Q1440

How is valve stem leakage controlled?

The answer is A. Valve packing must be properly compressed to prevent fluid loss and damage to the stem. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.5

Report a problem
Objective 1.2Q1441

What happens if valve packing is too tight?

The answer is D. If the packing is too tight, it will impair the movement and possibly damage the stem. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.5

Report a problem
Objective 1.2Q349

What is a likely effect of tightening a valve's packing to reduce leakage?

The answer is D. Tighter packing increases friction on the stem, requiring more force and possibly increasing stroke time or causing sticking. Approved lesson plan: Valve Fundamentals (Valve Fundamentals.docx), slide 1.61 Quiz - Packing

Gate and globe valves

Objectives 1.4, 1.5

"A gate valve is a linear motion valve used to start or stop fluid flow; however, it does not regulate or throttle flow." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.8

The disk is completely out of the flow stream when the valve is fully open, so it offers virtually no resistance to flow. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.8

"Hence, there is little pressure drop across an open gate valve." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.8
"Most of the flow change occurs near shutoff with a relatively high fluid velocity causing disk and seat wear and eventual leakage if used to regulate flow." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.10

Flow does not change evenly with stem travel, and a partly open gate disk tends to vibrate. For these reasons gate valves are not used to throttle. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.10

"A globe valve is a linear motion valve used to stop, start, and regulate fluid flow." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.15

The disk moves perpendicular to the seat, so the annular space closes gradually. This gives the globe valve good throttling ability. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.15

"When compared to a gate valve, a globe valve generally yields much less seat leakage." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.15
"The most evident shortcoming of the simple globe valve is the high head loss from two or more right angle turns of flowing fluid." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.15
"The backseat design prevents system pressure from building against the valve packing." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.18

Knowledge check: Gate and globe valves

Objective 1.5Q41

A gate valve is chosen when the system needs:

The answer is A. Gate valves have low resistance when fully open but are poor throttles. Globe valves are preferred for throttling. DOE-1018-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93), Types of Valves, ME-04 p. 43

Report a problem
Objective 1.5Q42

A globe valve is chosen for:

The answer is C. Globe valves throttle well and seal tightly, at the cost of higher head loss when open. DOE-1018-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93), Types of Valves, ME-04 p. 43

Report a problem
Objective 1.5Q1442

Why are gate valves not used to throttle flow?

The answer is A. Most of the flow change occurs near shutoff with a relatively high fluid velocity causing disk and seat wear and eventual leakage if used to regulate flow. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.10

Report a problem
Objective 1.5Q1443

What is the main drawback of a simple globe valve?

The answer is B. The most evident shortcoming of the simple globe valve is the high head loss from two or more right angle turns of flowing fluid. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.15

Report a problem
Objective 1.4Q1444

What does a globe valve backseat do?

The answer is B. The backseat design prevents system pressure from building against the valve packing. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.18

Ball and plug valves

Objectives 1.4, 1.5

"A ball valve is a rotational motion valve that uses a ball-shaped disk to stop or start fluid flow." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.18

Most ball valves need a 90° turn of the handle. When the handle lies along the axis of the valve, the valve is open. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.20

"A ball valve is generally the least expensive of any valve configuration and has low maintenance costs." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.19

Ball valves also offer quick, quarter turn on-off operation, are compact, require no lubrication, and give tight sealing with low torque. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.19

"Conventional ball valves have relatively poor throttling characteristics." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.19

In a throttling position the partly exposed seat erodes rapidly from high velocity flow. Elastomeric seats also keep these valves from elevated temperatures. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.19

"A plug valve is a rotational motion valve used to stop or start fluid flow." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.21

The passage in the plug lines up with the valve ports when open, and a 90° turn blocks them. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.21

"Multiport valves are particularly advantageous on transfer lines and for diverting services." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.22

One multiport valve can replace three or four shutoff valves, but many configurations do not completely shut off flow. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.22

Diaphragm, pinch, butterfly, needle, and reducing valves

Objectives 1.4, 1.5

"A diaphragm valve is a linear motion valve that is used to start, regulate, and stop fluid flow." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.24
"Diaphragm valves are particularly suited for the handling of corrosive fluids, fibrous slurries, radioactive fluids, or other fluids that must remain free from contamination." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.25

The operating mechanism is not exposed to the fluid, and there are no packing glands to maintain. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.25

"Pinch valves are suitable for on-off and throttling services." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.30

Pinch valves suit slurries and liquids with large amounts of suspended solids, because the operating mechanism is completely isolated from the fluid. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.30

"A butterfly valve, illustrated in Figure 19, is a rotary motion valve that is used to stop, regulate, and start fluid flow." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.31

A 90° rotation of the handle moves the disk from fully closed to fully open. Savings in weight, space, and cost are the most obvious advantages, especially for large valves. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.31

"Butterfly valves are especially well-suited for the handling of large flows of liquids or gases at relatively low pressures and for the handling of slurries or liquids with large amounts of suspended solids." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.32
"A needle valve, as shown in Figure 20, is used to make relatively fine adjustments in the amount of fluid flow." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.33

The long, tapered point acts as a disk and passes through the orifice before it seats, so the opening changes very gradually. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.33

"Reducing valves automatically reduce supply pressure to a preselected pressure as long as the supply pressure is at least as high as the selected pressure." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.28

An adjusting spring pushes against a diaphragm, and reduced outlet pressure opposes it. The balance positions the auxiliary valve, and so the main valve. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.29

Which valve suits fluids that must stay free of contamination, such as radioactive fluids?

Objective 1.5Q1448

Which valve is especially suited to large flows at relatively low pressures?

The answer is D. Butterfly valves are especially well-suited for the handling of large flows of liquids or gases at relatively low pressures. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.32

Report a problem
Objective 1.5Q1449

Which valve is used for relatively fine adjustments of flow?

The answer is D. A needle valve is used to make relatively fine adjustments in the amount of fluid flow. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.33

Objective 1.5Q1450

What does a reducing valve do?

A valve is a rubber sleeve squeezed by an external mechanism. What type is it?

Check valves

Objectives 1.4, 1.5

"Check valves are designed to prevent the reversal of flow in a piping system." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.35

Flow opens the valve, and any reversal of flow closes it. Closure comes from the weight of the check mechanism, back pressure, a spring, or a combination. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.35

A swing check gives full, unobstructed flow, and turbulence and pressure drop are very low. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.35

"Swing check valves are usually installed in conjunction with gate valves because they provide relatively free flow." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.36

Swing checks suit low velocity flow. Pulsating flow would make the disk flap and destroy the seating elements. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.36

"A lift check valve, illustrated in Figure 24, is commonly used in piping systems in which globe valves are being used as a flow control valve." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.37

Flow to a lift check must always enter below the seat. Backflow and gravity force the disk or ball onto the seat. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.38

"A stop check valve, illustrated in Figure 27, is a combination of a lift check valve and a globe valve." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.40

With the stem closed, the disk cannot leave the seat, as in a globe valve. With the stem open, the valve works as a lift check. The stem is not connected to the disk. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.40

Objective 1.5Q1452

What is the purpose of a check valve?

The answer is D. Check valves are designed to prevent the reversal of flow in a piping system. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.35

Objective 1.5Q1453

Why should swing check valves be kept off lines with pulsating flow?

The answer is D. They should not be used on lines with pulsating flow when the continual flapping or pounding would be destructive to the seating elements. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.36

What combination makes up a stop check valve?

Relief and safety valves

Objectives 1.4, 1.5

Relief and safety valves prevent equipment damage by relieving accidental over-pressurization of fluid systems. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.40

"The main difference between a relief valve and a safety valve is the extent of opening at the setpoint pressure." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.40

A relief valve gradually opens as inlet pressure rises above the setpoint, and only as far as needed. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.40

A safety valve rapidly pops fully open at the pressure setting and stays open until pressure drops below a reset pressure. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.40

"The difference between the actuating pressure setpoint and the pressure at which the safety valve resets is called blowdown." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.40

Blowdown is expressed as a percentage of the actuating pressure setpoint. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.40

"Relief valves are typically used for incompressible fluids such as water or oil." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.41

Safety valves are typically used for compressible fluids such as steam or other gases. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.41

"Safety valves can often be distinguished by the presence of an external lever at the top of the valve body, which is used as an operational check." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.41

Most of these valves open against a compression spring, and the adjusting nuts set the pressure. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.41

How does a safety valve open when its pressure setting is reached?

Safety valve blowdown is the difference between the actuating pressure and:

How can a safety valve often be told apart from a relief valve?

What is the main difference between a relief valve and a safety valve?

Manual actuators

Objectives 1.6

"Manual actuators are capable of placing the valve in any position but do not permit automatic operation." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.44

A handwheel fixed to the stem gives only the mechanical advantage of the wheel. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.44

A hammer handwheel moves freely through part of its turn and then hits a lug on a secondary wheel attached to the stem. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.45

"With this arrangement, the valve can be pounded shut for tight closure or pounded open if it is stuck shut." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.45

Gear heads add mechanical advantage, so one person can operate the valve, but operating time for large valves is exceptionally long. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.45

"All actuators except manual handwheel and lever are adaptable to automatic actuation." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.44

Power actuators

Objectives 1.6

"The motor is usually a, reversible, high speed type connected through a gear train to reduce the motor speed and thereby increase the torque at the stem." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.46

Direction of motor rotation sets direction of disk motion, and a handwheel can be engaged for manual operation. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.46

"Limit switches are normally provided to stop the motor automatically at full open and full closed valve positions." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.46
"These actuators translate an air signal into valve stem motion by air pressure acting on a diaphragm or piston connected to the stem." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.47

When air pressure closes the valve and spring action opens it, the actuator is direct-acting. When air pressure opens it and spring action closes it, the actuator is reverse-acting. Duplex actuators have air on both sides of the diaphragm. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.47

"These actuators use a piston to convert a signal pressure into valve stem motion." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.47

Hydraulic fluid is fed to one side of the piston while the other side is drained or bled. Solenoid valves typically direct the fluid. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.47

"Solenoids position the valve by attracting a magnetic slug attached to the valve stem." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.48

In a single solenoid valve, a spring acts against the slug, and removing power returns the valve to the opposite position. Fail open valves are opened by the spring and closed by energizing the solenoid. Fail closed valves are the reverse. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.48

"Double solenoid valves typically fail "as is."" DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.48
"In general, fastest actuation is provided by hydraulic, pneumatic, and solenoid actuators." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.49
"However, solenoids are not practical for large valves because their size and power requirements would be excessive." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.49
"Upon a loss of power, an MOV will fail as is." Word: Valve Fundamentals.docx, slide 1.47 Electric-Motor Actuator

In an electric motor valve actuator, the gear train between the motor and the valve stem:

A pneumatic actuator closes the valve with air pressure and opens it with a spring. What is it called?

In the pneumatic diaphragm actuator described in the lesson, what happens to the valve with no supply air?

Why are solenoids not used on large valves?

The answer is C. Solenoids are not practical for large valves because their size and power requirements would be excessive. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.49

Valve position and good operating practice

From the lesson plan

Remote position indication uses lights driven by a detector that senses stem, disk, or actuator position, such as a mechanical limit switch or a magnetic switch. Word: Valve Fundamentals.docx, slide 1.70 Valve Position Indication

Locally, a rising stem shows position, and nonrising stem and power actuated valves often use mechanical pointers. Word: Valve Fundamentals.docx, slide 1.70 Valve Position Indication

"Always open valves slowly to minimize system pressure transients." Word: Valve Fundamentals.docx, slide 1.54 Manual Valve Operation

Opening a valve slowly also lets the system stabilize as flow rates change. Use both hands where the design allows, and do not use unapproved aids such as cheater bars. Word: Valve Fundamentals.docx, slide 1.54 Manual Valve Operation

"Thermal binding is more likely to occur in a wedge gate valve that is closed while the system is hot." Word: Valve Fundamentals.docx, slide 1.57 Thermal Binding of Gate Valves

Parts of different materials and thicknesses cool at different rates. Yoke arms contract faster than the body and compress the stem, which causes the valve to bind. Word: Valve Fundamentals.docx, slide 1.57 Thermal Binding of Gate Valves

"Opening a valve results in increased flow and decreased backpressure as measured upstream of the valve." Word: Valve Fundamentals.docx, slide 1.63 Valve Position and Fluid Flow

Closing a valve results in decreased flow and increased backpressure upstream of the valve. Word: Valve Fundamentals.docx, slide 1.63 Valve Position and Fluid Flow

Worked examples

Objective 1.5

Safety valve blowdown

A safety valve lifts at 200 psig and reseats at 190 psig. Find the blowdown as a percentage of the actuating pressure.

  1. Blowdown is the difference between setpoint and reset pressure: 200 - 190 = 10 psig.
  2. Express it as a percentage of the setpoint: 10 / 200 x 100.

Answer: 5%.

DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.40

Objective 1.5

Relief valve setpoint

A spring holds a relief valve disk shut with 1000 lbf, and system pressure acts on 4 in² of disk area. At what pressure does the valve lift?

  1. The setpoint depends on spring force and the disk area on which pressure acts, so use P = F / A.
  2. P = 1000 lbf / 4 in² = 250 psi.

Answer: 250 psi.

Word: Valve Fundamentals.docx, slide 1.88 Valve Setpoint Calculation

Summary

  • A valve's basic parts are the body, bonnet, trim, actuator, and packing. Stem leakage is controlled by properly compressing the packing. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.7
  • Gate valves give low resistance but do not throttle. Globe valves throttle well but have high head loss. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.43
  • Ball valves give quarter turn on-off service, plug valves direct flow between ports, and diaphragm and pinch valves isolate the mechanism from the fluid. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.43
  • Check valves prevent reverse flow, and safety and relief valves provide automatic overpressure protection. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.43
  • Actuators are manual, electric motor, pneumatic, hydraulic, and solenoid. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-04 p.50
